newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bolsas halt Telebras receipts on Motta remarks.
newsitem.headline: Bolsas halt Telebras receipts on Motta remarks.

text.p: Brazilian bolsas said they halted trade in subscription receipts of Telebras after Communications Minister Sergio Motta said he would back a court ruling against the firm in a subscription receipt dispute.
"We halted trade in Telebras subscription receipts after Motta's comments," said a spokesman for the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).
Telebras receipts fell 12 percent on Motta's comments before trading was suspended, traders said.
Telebras is awaiting a final court ruling, which Motta said could take years, on whether holders of Telebras subscription receipts will be issued preferred shares from a 1990 public offering.

In October last year, a regional federal court judge ruled in favor of the subscription receipt holders, rejecting a government appeal in 1992 to block the issue based on allegations the offering was undervalued.
The government, which is Telebras' majority shareholder, is appealing the decision. Motta told reporters a court ruling recognizing the share issue would cost the government 1.0 billion reais.
The Communications Ministry also said that, even if the justices rule in favor of the firm, the decision should be submitted to the company's shareholders.
"The final ruling can take one, two, three years, and it has to be submitted and approved by the shareholders. And we (the government) are the majority shareholders," he said.
